title: Two Panels
youtube_title: Charges filed. She engraves the first two panels of evidence
logline: The prosecutor files the pickup log and the examiner's report. Nora engraves the first two panels, breaks down on the word "Pills," and gives the left-hand lead to the prosecutor. Peg stays at the wall with a slip of paper.
hook: The prosecutor's filing notice goes up on the light box. Nora reads it aloud: "Two exhibits." "The pickup log." "The examiner's report." Beside the rack she pins a sketch: the outline of a left hand. She picks up the engraving pen.
mid_hook: The pen reaches the word "Pills." Her hand shakes, stops. The pen drops on the bench. She slides down the brick wall and sobs out loud. Sparks freezes. Peg doesn't go to her. "Pick it up." "Spell it right."
extra_hooks: Both panels slide into the first two slots. Sparks, barely a whisper: "Two down." "Ten to go." Peg, not looking up: "Good at math, aren't you."
conflict: The wall finally holds something, but only two of twelve, and the first word is the thing that took her baby. And whose left hand traced her name? She won't chase Sienna or confront anyone; what she saw goes to the prosecutor. Peg stands at the wall and won't leave.
turn: Before the panels go up she calls Dana: "The report says left-handed." "Sienna signs left-handed. I saw it." Dana: "Then Reyes hears it. Not Sienna." You think that call ends the night. The real thing happens after everyone leaves: alone at the wall, Peg slits open the cover of her ledger.

cliffhanger.text: Late night, only the furnace glow. Peg is still at the wall. From a slit in the ledger's cover she pulls a tiny folded slip and holds it a long time. She turns. "Nora." "The third panel." "What goes on it?"
cliffhanger.question: Will Peg hand over that slip?

spectacle: Two engraved panels slot into the first two places on the twelve-slot steel rack; Number Three's firelight passes through the engraving and throws soft, blurred strokes of light across the red brick (the words are added in post).
glamour_shot: She bends over the glass with the engraving pen, goggles pushed up, sleeves rolled, cheeks still wet; with every stroke the furnace light jumps on her lashes.
general_payoffs: The first two panels go up on the evidence wall: "Pills: pharmacy pickup log" and "Signature: examiner's report" (text added in post)

title: I Was One Day Late
youtube_title: She hid the receipt 5 months. Then she told the whole call
logline: At the evidence wall, Peg tells what she has hidden for five months: Grant's call past midnight the night Nora lost the baby, the receipt in his car the next day, and her own night in that hallway thirty-four years ago. Nora explodes, then they hold each other and cry.
hook: Peg flattens the slip on the light box. A confectionery receipt (shown as an insert card, text added in post). She reads it out flat: "Prop tablets." "A hundred." "The day you left the hospital." "It was in his car."
mid_hook: "The night you lost the baby," "he called me. Past midnight." "'If Nora asks,'" "'I was with you all night.'" "Before he hung up," "he said to someone else," "'That thing's taken care of.'"
extra_hooks: Nora shoots to her feet. "Five months?" "Reyes threw me out!" "I couldn't pay for the room!" "You had this the whole time!" Peg shouts back: "He's my son!" "You think I wanted it true?"
conflict: Hand this over and she is a mother testifying against her own son. She has kept it five months, through the declined report and the motel bills, watching her daughter-in-law dig alone while the proof sat in her ledger.
turn: You think Peg kept quiet to protect her son. She kept quiet because she already knew, and couldn't admit the boy she raised could do it. She left with Nora because thirty-four years ago, nobody left with her.

cliffhanger.text: Peg grips the light box and breaks. "Thirty-four years ago" "I sat in that hallway all night." "His father never came." She pushes the receipt across. "I'm not helping you." "I'm helping that baby." "I found it the next day." "I was one day late." Nora pulls her in; Peg clutches her sweater and sobs out loud, and Nora cries with her.
cliffhanger.question: Can this receipt sink him?

spectacle: The light box glows up through a crumpled receipt, the paper itself shining white between two faces wet with tears; the printed lines are a flat insert card added in post.
glamour_shot: Nora and Peg holding each other at the light box, Nora's shoulder-length hair against Peg's worn cardigan, both shaking; the furnace lights them from behind and their shadows merge into one on the brick.
general_payoffs: Why Peg left with her is revealed: past midnight the night Nora lost the baby, Grant called Peg ("If Nora asks, I was with you all night") and she heard him tell someone else, "That thing's taken care of." The day Nora left the hospital, Peg found a receipt in his car from a confectionery that makes prop candy: "Prop tablets, qty 100." Thirty-four years ago she sat alone all night in the same Merrow General hallway
Nora screams at Peg for hiding it five months, then they hold each other and cry

title: Then I Keep This One
youtube_title: His own mother slams the ledger down: "Put me on the stand"
logline: Nora takes Peg and the receipt to the prosecutor. Reyes will subpoena the confectionery, but that takes weeks; he bags the original and gives Peg a copy, Peg demands to testify, and Reyes lets slip that Grant's lawyer came asking whether Nora will still testify.
hook: The prosecutor's office. Reyes holds the receipt under his desk lamp a long time. "Order number's real." "I'll subpoena the shop." "Takes weeks." "Till then, it's a receipt."
mid_hook: Peg slams the ledger on his desk. "I'm his mother." "I heard him." "Put me on the stand." Reyes holds a beat, glances at Nora. "You will." "But 'that thing' could be anything."
extra_hooks: In the corridor Peg slows down. Quietly: "When he broke a dish as a boy," "he did this too." "Hid it first."
conflict: The receipt proves someone bought a hundred prop tablets, not who. She can't go question the confectionery herself; the subpoena takes weeks, and the original has to stay with the prosecutor.
turn: She thinks she has been turned away again. But Reyes bags the original, labels it, and hands Peg a photocopy; Peg folds it into her ledger cover: "Then I keep this one." "Till there's a name." And his last line shows her the board: Grant is scared.

cliffhanger.text: As they stand to go, Reyes closes the file without looking up. "Oh. One thing." "His lawyer came by today." "Asked if you'd still testify."
cliffhanger.question: Why is Grant rushing her?

spectacle: Under the desk lamp, a crumpled receipt slides into a clear evidence bag on a thick case file; Reyes presses the label down and the light catches the plastic.
glamour_shot: She walks Peg down the long corridor of the prosecutor's office, shoulder-length hair, dark coat, the fluorescent lights sliding back over their heads; her step is steadier than Peg's.
general_payoffs: Reyes takes the receipt seriously: the order number is real and he will subpoena the confectionery's records; the original stays in evidence, Peg keeps a copy

title: Number Three Can't Go Cold
youtube_title: The ferry night moves up, and the old furnace man goes down
logline: The ferry terminal moves its maiden voyage up with twelve blue panels still unblown; that same night Gus throws out his back hauling cullet alone, refuses the ambulance, and Number Three can't be allowed to go cold.
hook: Fiona stands in Remelt's doorway with the spec binder. "The maiden voyage" "moved up to next Friday." Sparks looks at the half-built chandelier on the rack. "We've still got twelve…"
mid_hook: Past nine. Gus hauls a sack of cullet alone, locks up halfway bent, and eases himself down beside the spilled glass. "My back."
extra_hooks: Sparks calls 911. Two EMTs check Gus on the cot: "Back spasm. Rest." Gus waves off the stretcher and signs the refusal. "The furnace." "Can't go cold." "It goes cold," "the brick cracks."
conflict: Twelve panels in eight days. If Number Three goes cold, its twelve-year-old brick could crack through. Only Gus knows how to tend it, and she still can't go near a hot furnace.
turn: She thought the deadline was the hard part. It's people: the only blower is a twenty-year-old apprentice, the man who keeps the fire is down, and she can't touch the furnace.

cliffhanger.text: Gus on the cot, gripping her sleeve. "If I'm down," "who watches the fire" "tonight?" Number Three roars on. The old wall clock chimes ten.
cliffhanger.question: Who keeps Number Three lit?

spectacle: In Number Three's firelight a sack of cullet spills across the floor, rounded, blunt blue and clear pebbles of glass, and an old man sits beside the spill, not on it; no cuts, no redness on hands.
glamour_shot: She crouches beside Gus with a hand on his back, her apron dusted pale, and looks back at the roaring furnace; for the first time her eyes show a flicker of panic.
general_payoffs: EMTs check Gus (back spasm, rest); he refuses transport and stays on the cot by the furnace

title: The Man in the Heat Gloves
youtube_title: Who watches the furnace? Her contract husband walks in
logline: With no one to tend Number Three, Elias shows up at night in heat gloves; for seven nights he watches the temperature and the gas and never touches her chandelier, while Nora calls the moves and Sparks charges the furnace and blows panel after panel.
hook: Ten p.m. The steel door swings open: Elias in work clothes, thick heat gloves on both hands. "Gus called me." Gus lifts a hand from the cot. "Mr. Ashford." "The fire's yours."
mid_hook: "You know how?" He checks the temperature gauge and eases the gas valve. "Gus taught me." Nora: "Charge it." Elias steps back from the furnace mouth; Sparks takes the shovel.
extra_hooks: 2 a.m. Theo sneaks in with takeout, typing on his tablet. "Mrs. Ashford Observation Log." "Two a.m." "Boss is babysitting a furnace."
conflict: She has to finish twelve panels and can't let Elias touch her chandelier: clause two. Tending the fire is the landlord's furnace and a favor for Gus; which panel gets blown, and how, belongs to her and Sparks.
turn: She expects him to pitch in on the rush. For seven nights he does exactly one thing: keeps the fire. Three identical shots: the rack fuller each time, the window going from black to grey, Theo's takeout boxes stacked higher. The chandelier is hers, the furnace is his, and he never crosses that line.

cliffhanger.text: Dawn on the seventh day, twenty-three blue panels on the rack. She hands Sparks the blowpipe. "Last one." "All yours." "I won't call it." Sparks's grip on the pipe shakes.
cliffhanger.question: Can Sparks do it without her?

spectacle: Remelt at night: a gloved figure crouches at the gas valve while Sparks feeds the furnace mouth, and the firelight throws the tall shadow across the whole evidence wall, over the two engraved panels.
glamour_shot: Elias, work sleeves rolled to the forearm, pushes the furnace door shut in thick gloves; his thin-framed glasses catch the fire and sweat runs down his temple. He doesn't look back.
general_payoffs: Number Three never goes cold: Elias keeps the fire seven nights straight, and Sparks does every charge

title: Straight: 1
youtube_title: 24 crooked tries later, he blows the last panel alone
logline: Sparks blows the last blue panel on his own and it comes out straight; all twenty-four panels are done, but one call from the ferry terminal adds a guest to the maiden voyage.
hook: Arms folded behind the safety line, she says nothing. Sparks gathers, turns, blows; Gus watches, propped up on the cot. The glass comes out. Three seconds of silence. Sparks: "...It's straight?" Nora: "It's straight."
mid_hook: Sparks racks the pipe, rips off his goggles, roars, and throws his arms around Gus. "My back!" Gus laughs and cries at once. Sparks slashes chalk beside a long row of tally marks: "Straight! One!" Behind the line, Nora covers her mouth, eyes wet.
extra_hooks: Before dawn the twenty-four blue panels go into wooden crates one by one. By the furnace there's only a pair of heat gloves on the floor. Elias is already gone.
conflict: If the last panel comes out crooked, they miss tomorrow night's maiden voyage. She has to keep her mouth shut and let Sparks stand up there alone.
turn: She thought she wouldn't be able to stay quiet, and she never makes a sound. His first straight piece is what she taught him, and it's his own.

cliffhanger.text: Fiona calls. "The maiden voyage sponsor" "is Whitlock Home." "Mr. Whitlock" "is giving a speech." She looks at the twenty-four crates and says nothing.
cliffhanger.question: Grant on her big night?

spectacle: Remelt before dawn: twenty-four panels of early-morning harbor blue lined up on the wooden rack; the first daylight comes through the high windows and all twenty-four light up at once.
glamour_shot: She stands behind the safety line with her arms folded, goggles up on her head, biting her lip as Sparks blows the last panel; when the glass comes out, her eyes smile first.

title: The Court Will Give It Back
youtube_title: She won't shake her ex's hand. Two lines, and the room claps
logline: Maiden voyage night: twenty-four blue panels light the terminal and the blind review is read out, "Remelt. Nora Quinn." She walks up, won't shake Grant's hand, says two lines into the mic; a reporter asks him about forgery. Afterward he puts an offer in writing.
hook: The terminal hall goes dark, and twenty-four blue panels light up at once, hanging like dawn waves rolling in over the harbor. Silhouettes tilt their heads back. Nobody says a word.
mid_hook: Fiona at the mic. "It was a blind review." "The jury didn't know whose it was." "Remelt. Nora Quinn." A spotlight swings to the last row: her, in her work jacket. Three faces turn. Then four.
extra_hooks: She walks up. At the sponsor's spot Grant puts out his hand. She doesn't take it. Into the mic: "Six years, I designed for a brand." "Tonight my name's on it." Applause. His smile locks. Lyle calls out: "Mr. Whitlock, are you charged with forgery?" His PR man steers him off.

After the crowd, she presses a wedding ring into Peg's palm. "The first ferry check." "I got it back." Peg: "Who asked you to?" She puts it on, turns away, shoulders shaking, wipes her eyes on her sleeve. "Stupid ring."
conflict: It's her first work hung in a public space, and Grant is the sponsor: he means to stand under her light and talk up his brand, and to shake her hand for the cameras.
turn: Grant thinks the sponsor's podium lets him make the chandelier his. Then her name is read out, she won't take his hand, and the only question the press asks him is about a forgery charge.

cliffhanger.text: In the car, Grant calls. "Drop the civil suit." "Don't testify." "The house is yours." "The court will give it back." She hangs up. He texts the same offer (text added in post); she forwards it to Dana. Dana: "He just put it in writing." Another text. She reads it aloud: "Then I'll come to you." "Face to face."
cliffhanger.question: Is he coming to her door?

title: As Long as It's Lit
youtube_title: Her ex wants a meeting. She picks the place: her own studio
logline: Nora sets the meeting at Remelt for Thursday; Dana warns Elias he can't fight her battles, he says he's only tending the furnace; Peg demands to come and is told she's a witness, not backup; that night at the fire Elias says something that doesn't sound like a contract.
hook: She types, saying it aloud: "Remelt." "Thursday, eight." On the phone Dana's voice jumps. "What are you negotiating?" "I'm not." "I'm letting him look."
mid_hook: Top floor of Ashford Construction. Dana slaps a file on the desk. "You can't fight for her." Elias doesn't look up. "I won't." "Gus is still laid up." "I tend the furnace." Theo quietly logs it: "Boss." "Furnace."
extra_hooks: The Ashford house. Peg stabs her knitting needles into the table. "I made him." "I get to look him in the eye." Nora: "Not yet." "You're my witness, not my backup." Peg grits her teeth, gathers the needles. "Then you come home" "and eat your stew."
conflict: Grant is coming to her place to bargain. She won't let anyone speak for her, Peg has to stay clean for the stand, and she knows that on Thursday it won't be just the two of them in that shop.
turn: She expects Elias to keep his distance under clause two. He says he'll be there: not beside her, at the furnace. It's his furnace. He'd be there anyway.

cliffhanger.text: Late night, only the furnace light. Elias, in heat gloves, watches the gauge. She sets a bowl of pasta on the steel stool beside him; without looking he says, "Salty." She laughs. "Thursday," "you'll be here?" Eyes on the fire: "As long as it's lit," "I'm here."

mid_hook: The engine dies outside. Dress shoes on gravel, step by step. Sparks, low: "Should I" "shut the door?" "Let him in." "Let him look."

title: Hello, Sales. Twelve Years.
youtube_title: Her ex mocks two panels. Then the man at the furnace turns
logline: Grant looks at two panels of glass, tells Nora to drop the case and says she can't beat him alone; he never sees it coming when the figure at the furnace turns around and brings back his name from twelve years ago.
hook: Grant's first time inside Remelt. He takes in the brick, the bead stopped at Charges, stops at the evidence wall, taps the first panel with his glass cufflink and smiles. "Two panels of glass." "Drop it, Nor." "You can't beat me alone."
mid_hook: He steps closer, voice soft. "Men like him" "don't do favors, Nor." Her blowpipe keeps turning. "I know." "I'm using him too." At the furnace, Elias's gloved hand stops on the valve. Then moves again.
extra_hooks: She looks at the twelve slots. "Twelve." "The day they're full," "you get sentenced." He laughs. "Twelve?" "You don't even have a third."
conflict: Grant wants the case dropped tonight. He has lawyers, money and the press; she has two panels of glass. She has to show him she won't drop it and isn't afraid, without knowing what lies between him and the man at the furnace.
turn: Grant thinks he came to tidy up an ex-wife. He needles her, laughs at her two panels, and never once notices the figure at the furnace until that man turns around.

cliffhanger.text: Elias turns from the furnace and pulls off his heat glove: on the back of his left hand, a pale, flat, silvery old burn scar. Grant's smile freezes. "...You." Elias: "Hello, Sales." "Twelve years." Nora's blowpipe stops mid-air. Only people from Pell's ever called him that.
